concepts.explanation: Perfect squares always have an odd total factor count because the factor pair (√x, √x) consists of identical numbers.

properties.statement: Perfect squares can only end in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. They never end in 2, 3, 7, or 8.

properties.property_name: Sum of First n Odd Numbers

properties.statement: There are exactly 2n non-square numbers between n^2 and (n+1)^2.

rules.formula_or_statement: A number is divisible by 2 if its unit digit is 0, 2, 4, 6, or 8.
A number is divisible by 3 (or 9) if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3 (or 9).
A number is divisible by 4 if the number formed by its last two digits is divisible by 4.
A number is divisible by 5 if its unit digit is 0 or 5; divisible by 10 if unit digit is 0.
A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.
Divide both antecedent and consequent by their Highest Common Factor (HCF).

procedures.title: Prime Factorisation Method for Square Roots
steps: Step 1: Resolve the given natural number into its prime factors.
Step 2: Group identical prime factors into pairs.
Step 3: Select one prime factor from each pair.
Step 4: Multiply the selected prime factors together to obtain the square root.

procedures.title: Prime Factorisation Method for Cube Roots
steps: Step 1: Resolve the given natural number into its prime factors.
Step 2: Group identical prime factors into triplets.
Step 3: Select one prime factor from each triplet.
Step 4: Multiply the selected prime factors together to obtain the cube root.

procedures.title: Constructing a Square given Diagonal length (No Protractor)
steps: Step 1: Draw diagonal line segment AC of specified length.
Step 2: Construct the perpendicular bisector of AC, intersecting at midpoint O.
Step 3: With center O and radius equal to half the diagonal, draw arcs on both sides of the bisector to mark vertices B and D.
Step 4: Connect AB, BC, CD, and DA to form square ABCD.

procedures.title: Converting a Decimal Number to Base-5 System
steps: Step 1: Divide the decimal number by 5 and record quotient and remainder.
Step 2: Continue dividing quotients by 5 until the quotient becomes 0.
Step 3: Read remainders in reverse order (bottom to top) to obtain the Base-5 representation.

procedures.title: Solving Proportional Word Problems via Unit Rate Method
steps: Step 1: Identify the given quantity and total cost/amount.
Step 2: Divide total amount by total quantity to find the rate per 1 unit.
Step 3: Multiply the unit rate by the target quantity required.
